newsitem.title: USA: Democrats won't file pre-election funding report.
newsitem.headline: Democrats won't file pre-election funding report.

text.p: The Democratic National Committee will not file a pre-election report detailing its contributions and spending for the first time in the 22 years since the federal election law was written, the Washington Post reported in its Tuesday's edition.
The pre-election report covers spending in the first two weeks of October and is the last public accounting of a candidate or political party's financial situation before the election.
The Republican National Committee's pre-election report said it took in about $25 million and spent $38 million, according to the Post.

DNC general counsel Joseph Sandler told the newspaper the party wasn't required to file the report because it didn't spend any money directly on behalf of President Bill Clinton or other candidates during that time. He said "cash flow" concerns led the DNC to hold off on such spending.

The DNC's decision not to file a report came after two weeks of intense media scrutiny of its fundraising amid questions about whether the party had solicited or accepted illegal contributions from foreigners or other sources.

RNC Chairman Haley Barbour said in an interview with the Post that the DNC was reflecting "the utter contempt that this administration and its political arm have for the law, the public's right to know and the media's ability to make disclosure meaningful."
